messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

I want a fair financial share, and I won’t subsidize A buying the house at a discount. I want us to settle it fairly without damaging my relationship with my twin, but I’m not in a rush. I haven’t agreed to a discounted purchase. My objections aren’t just about A’s husband, though he does make this harder.
I’d like to buy the house with my husband at a family discount. The price and terms aren’t settled, and I can’t proceed without C’s agreement. What nags at me is that she hasn’t agreed yet.

Thank you. I’d like the money side to leave me with enough to get a dance studio started. I hope we can settle things fairly, though I’m not sure what that would mean in amounts yet. I suppose my small worry is that there may not be enough left for the studio.
Yes, that fits. No need to add anything about A’s husband. I’d rather get it right than rush.

Mostly, but I’d put it this way: I want to buy the house at a family discount, and I need C’s agreement to do that. I’m not just trying to stop waiting. I can’t say about a cost to C without knowing what you mean; I don’t want to proceed over her objection.

That wording fits. I’m not sure which of those reasons best explains the discount; I haven’t said the house would be unaffordable without it. I do want the chance to buy it with my husband at a family discount.
The first wording fits. The worry is more that there may not be enough left to start the studio; I’m not especially worried about how long it takes. I don’t know what figure would be enough yet.
I’m not sure what I’d lose at full appraised value; I don’t know whether we could afford it. The discount matters to whether buying is workable for us, but I can’t say more than that.
